beats.hook: My uncle stood up at my grandmother's funeral and said, "She wasn't your mother, Carol. She was mine."
beats.setup: Carol is my mom. She had no idea what was coming. None of us did.
beats.incident: My grandmother — Nana Ruth — had just been buried an hour before. We were back at the house, eating casserole, grieving normally. Then Uncle Dennis just — stood up. Set down his plate. And said it out loud, in front of everyone. What I couldn't figure out was why he had waited until she was in the ground.
beats.escalation: Turns out Nana Ruth had made him promise to stay quiet while she was alive. Dennis had known for thirty years. My mom was actually born to Dennis's teenage girlfriend — a girl Nana Ruth took the baby from, quietly, and raised as her own. The girlfriend had never stopped looking for her.
beats.payoff: My mom went pale. Then she asked one question: "Is she still alive?" Dennis nodded. He pulled out his phone — and there was already a message. The woman had been waiting. She had sent it the morning of the funeral.
beats.cta: My mom has a biological mother who's been searching for her for decades — and I don't know if she's going to respond. Would you?
